pr_title: samples: fix the metairq_dispatch sample sporadically failed on ehl_crb
pr_body:
The metairq sample sometimes failed due to stuck because it has a
potential race when recording the latencies. The previous solution
checks whether the stats.mirq greater than MAX_EVENT. But stats.mirq
might also have a race here. So we change to check the msg sequence,
its correctness ensured by the kernel's message queue.

And also remove the spinlock in previous fix because tests only use
1 CPU, no need to add this. It also improves the fix for #40889,
to prevent test failed sporadically on acrn_ehl_crb and ehl_crb.	

Fix #42874.

Signed-off-by: Enjia Mai <enjia.mai@intel.com>

issue_context.title: ehl_crb: samples/kernel/metairq_dispatch fails when it is run multiple times
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The sample samples/kernel/metairq_dispatch runs failed on ehl_crb

**To Reproduce**

1. source zephyr-env.sh
2. twister -W -p ehl_crb --device-testing --device-serial /dev/ttyUSB0 -T samples/kernel/metairq_dispatch/ --west-flash=/home/ztest/EHL_X86_PXE.sh -j 1 -vvv
3. Sample passes when run for the first time and fails when we re-run again.

**Expected behavior**
The sample should run successfully and console output should show a complete statistical message.

review_comments: I'd still prefer to see a root cause here, and don't understand why the previous fix with the spinlock wasn't correct.  But this looks safe as I read it.

I'm confused here.  I'm just now noticing the earlier patch, but... it looks correct to me.  This is a test of preemptible thread behavior, so locking of some form between the threads is probably what we want.

But to be clear: it doesn't have to be a spinlock.  There's no ISR context and (as you point out) we're running with MP_NUM_CPUS=1, so anything will do: a k_mutex() or k_sem() would be fine, and (as long as we're never SMP) so would sched_un/lock().

Yes, @andyross , in previous patch I did not aware of this is a 1 CPU scenario, like you pointing out, it only does irq_lock here, and no ISR context. (Actually I tried it doesn't work at all to fix this issue).  So the spinlock should be removed here.

And I try on another way to fix this, by just checking if the message sequence number > MAX_EVENT) when entering the record_latencies subroutine  (in previously I check the stats.mirq but it still failed sometimes due to this shared variable can also have a race. 

Look like it works well and no need to protect a section of code. And I tested it on both ehl_crb and acrn_ehl_crb then the test pass more than 20 times. Actually this failure can be reproduced within 5~8 times previously.

Do you think is this solution ok? Thank you!
